cultural.vision_reason: This is a hand-woven, strip-cloth cotton gown (tobe/boubou) with hand embroidery, a garment type historically associated with Wolof and other West African (Senegambian) tailors and wearers; the form and technique are consistent with the claim.

physical.title: gown; tobe
physical.summary: Gown (tobe, boubou) formed from thirteen narrow strips of hand-spun off-white cotton used in both warp and weft. It has been hand-woven and hand-sewn together along the selvedges. The gown is not tailored: the cloth is hemmed at both ends, folded in two, a hole cut for the head, and the sides sewn together. The gown has been extensively embroidered on both sides with geometric patterns including crossed square and circles, using imported European coloured threads. There are three identifiable forms of stitch: herringbone (in light and dark blue, gold and pink dyed cotton), knot stitch (in green and pink dyed cotton) and loop stitch (natural cotton coloured cotton). There are also two areas of appliqué consisting of arcs of pink tightly woven cotton, one around the collar, the other adjacent to the collar.
